function.mechanism: Reduces surface tension and destabilizes foam films, suppressing persistent foam during food processing.
common_food_categories: Processed foods with controlled defoaming during manufacture
Dry gelatin dessert mixes (with ready-to-serve limit)
Salt labeled for cooking purposes (with cooked-food limit)
Fruit juice processing contexts referenced in CFR standards

adi.basis: EFSA FAF Panel re-evaluation (2020) established ADI 17 mg/kg bw/day from a rat NOAEL (1,742 mg/kg bw/day) with uncertainty factor 100; prior ADI 1.5 mg/kg bw/day withdrawn.

efsa.key_finding: EFSA concluded no safety concern at reported uses and use levels; estimated dietary exposures did not exceed the ADI.

fda.notes: Listed for use in defoaming agents with a general maximum of 10 ppm in food (and specified exceptions/ready-to-consume limits).

adi.basis: JECFA records reviewed show an ADI range of 0-17 mg/kg bw/day (74th meeting context).

concerns.summary: Corneal effects were reported in rat studies but interpreted by EFSA as local contact effects from feed/feces rather than systemic toxicity.
Recent PubMed-indexed literature is sparse for additive-specific human dietary safety, creating uncertainty driven by data gaps rather than a strong harm signal.

no_concern_confirmed: EFSA reported very limited gastrointestinal absorption and predominantly unchanged fecal excretion.
EFSA reported no genotoxicity concern for E900.
EFSA concluded estimated dietary exposures across evaluated scenarios did not exceed ADI 17 mg/kg bw/day.
JECFA records reviewed are consistent with an ADI range up to 17 mg/kg bw/day.

populations: none identified in EFSA exposure scenarios
adi_exceedance.notes: EFSA reported that exposure estimates for evaluated population groups/scenarios did not exceed the ADI of 17 mg/kg bw/day.

risk_assessment.rationale: E900 is approved by major regulators with an established ADI and clear conditions of use; EFSA's re-evaluation found no safety concern at reported use levels and exposure estimates below ADI. Residual uncertainty is mainly due to limited newer additive-specific human evidence, not strong demonstrated harm.
key_factors: EFSA 2020 ADI establishment at 17 mg/kg bw/day and no safety concern conclusion
FDA/eCFR explicit use conditions under 21 CFR 173.340
JECFA listing indicates ADI 0-17 mg/kg bw/day (2011 context)
No specific IARC classification found for dimethylpolysiloxane in checked agents-classified resources
PubMed search indicates sparse modern additive-specific oral safety studies
